Patient feels hot and sweaty but has not measured temperature: "I'm just being quite hot and sweaty" and "I felt a bit hot and sweaty, but I haven't really measured it."
Nausea without vomiting is reported: Doctor: "have you noticed any vomiting or feeling nauseous at all?" Patient: "Just a little nauseous, but no vomiting."
Increased urinary frequency: "I did notice I was going to the... I was peeing more regularly" and repeated: "just that I'm peeing more than off, more regularly."
Pink urine suggesting possible hematuria: "I did notice that I was a little. The urine was a little pink in color" and when asked about blood: "I can't say. I mean, maybe."

No vomiting: "Just a little nauseous, but no vomiting, no Vomiting?"

Clinician summary matches: abdominal pain for last couple days below belly button, pink urine, mild nausea, hot and sweaty, no dysuria or vomiting are all explicitly discussed in HPI and summarized: "for the last couple of days, this tummy pain... You notice some pink urine, but no burning or stinging... You felt a little bit nauseous and feeling hot and sweaty."

Doctor prescribes trimethoprim but specifies "We take two tablets, one tablet twice a day for three days," not "one tablet twice daily"; the phrasing "two tablets" vs "one" is inconsistent and unclear, so the specific regimen stated in the fact conflicts with the transcript wording.
Paracetamol recommended: "You can try just regular painkillers. Paracetamol will be advisable."
Hydration advised: "Make sure you drink plenty of fluids."
Cranberry juice suggested: "You can try some cranberry juice as well, which can sometimes help with your urine symptoms."
Pregnancy test recommended: "Maybe worth doing pregnancy tests later on just to confirm that" and reiterated as something to bear in mind.
